channel.title: Leónida Hoy — The GTA VI morning briefing
channel.description: The 5 GTA VI stories that matter today, each with a linked source and explained in plain words. Every morning.

item.title: Take-Two: GTA VI made $3.79 billion between preorders and day one
item.description:
An official Take-Two figure, review bombing in user scores while the press holds a 99, and a bug that closes the game on PS5. No official copies-sold number.

  1. Take-Two: GTA VI made $3.79 billion between preorders and day one. According to Variety, Take-Two says GTA VI preorders and first-day sales added up to $3.79 billion, and calls it "the biggest entertainment launch in history." A spokesperson wouldn't say how many copies were sold. Variety
  2. Metacritic: the press holds a 99, but users sink the score. Insider Gaming reports GTA VI is still at 99 out of 100 after 152 press reviews, but that about half of user scores are 49 or below, pointing to possible review bombing. Insider Gaming
  3. A bug is closing GTA VI on PS5 and sending some players back to the menu. According to DualShockers, a bug is closing the game on PS5 mid-session. Neither Sony nor Rockstar has given a cause or a fix, and reports point only to PS5. DualShockers

item.title: Rockstar announces GTA VI is available; Sensor Tower estimates 19 million copies
item.description:
An estimated 19 million copies on day one and sign-in problems on PSN. A group claims to have released an unauthenticated Xbox build, and a house hidden in 2021 turns up in the map.

  1. Rockstar announces GTA VI is now available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar and Take-Two have officially announced GTA VI is now available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Take-Two's press release presents it as the highest-rated game of all time on those platforms, the publisher's own framing. Rockstar Games
  2. GTA VI reportedly sold about 19 million copies on day one (estimate). Sensor Tower estimates about 19.1 million copies sold by the morning of launch, per Men's Journal, versus GTA V's record of 11 million in 24 hours. Take-Two hasn't confirmed figures. Another estimate says 17.1 million. Men's Journal
  3. PlayStation Network sign-in problems during GTA VI's launch. PS5 players have had trouble signing in to PlayStation Network during launch, per Cybernews and Happy Gamer. Sony hasn't explained the cause and Rockstar hasn't issued a statement. One source mentions a mandatory PS5 system update. Cybernews

item.title: GTA 6 is on sale: it unlocks at local midnight in each time zone
item.description:
After 13 years of waiting, GTA VI launches today on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S with record press scores. Preload demand spiked internet traffic in some regions.

  1. GTA 6 is on sale: it unlocks at local midnight in each time zone. After 13 years of waiting, GTA VI launches today, November 19, on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. NBC News reports sales are expected to top $1 billion (estimate) and that some people have called in sick to play. NBC News
  2. GTA VI preload demand spiked internet traffic in some regions. Dexerto reports the rush to preload the game caused traffic spikes on home networks: in some regions broadband use rose by more than 50%, according to a report. It's a third-party figure. Dexerto

item.title: GTA 6 now has a score: 99 on Metacritic and 98 on OpenCritic hours before launch
item.description:
First reviews are excellent: 99 on Metacritic and 98 on OpenCritic. A fake letter about a delay to 2027 is also debunked and the 2022 leak's author will be sentenced on the 23rd.

  1. GTA 6 review scores: embargo expected today, and store ratings don't count. Several outlets point to the review embargo lifting today, November 18, a day before launch. Rockstar hasn't confirmed any schedule. The ratings already showing on console stores come from buyers and aren't press reviews. Insider Gaming
  2. A Rockstar letter about a GTA VI delay to 2027 is fake. A Lead Stories fact check, relayed by Yahoo Tech, concludes a circulating letter saying the game is delayed to 2027 is fake. It found no such announcement on Rockstar's website. The date is still November 19. Yahoo Tech

item.title: Nearly 90% of preorders reportedly for the Ultimate edition, per a report (estimate)
item.description:
Two third-party estimates on GTA VI's business two days before launch: the Ultimate edition's share of preorders and Morgan Stanley's forecast of 40 million copies.

  1. Nearly 90% of preorders reportedly for the Ultimate edition, per a report. Shacknews relays a report saying nearly 90% of GTA VI preorders are for the Ultimate edition ($99.99 in the US). It's a third-party estimate: Rockstar and Take-Two don't publish preorder figures. Shacknews

item.title: GTA VI reportedly targets 30 fps on consoles, PS5 Pro included, three days before launch
item.description:
Several outlets agree the game will run at 30 fps even on PS5 Pro, and the preload open since November 10 came with a teaser featuring a Tove Lo track.

  1. GTA VI reportedly targets 30 fps on consoles, PS5 Pro included. Several outlets say Rockstar is aiming for a stable 30 fps on consoles, PS5 Pro included. TweakTown adds that its tech team is still unsure about a 60 fps mode. We couldn't check Rockstar's original statement. TweakTown

item.title: GTA VI will be playable on Xbox cloud from 7 a.m. Spain time on the 19th
item.description:
Xbox cloud play with limits, warnings about boxed-edition and PS5 codes, and three unconfirmed rumors about multiplayer, budget and review copies.

  1. GTA VI reaches Xbox cloud at 1:00 a.m. ET on November 19. Microsoft says the game will be playable by streaming on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S from 1:00 a.m. ET on the 19th (7:00 a.m. in Spain). It runs at Xbox Series S settings and isn't planned for PC, phones or TVs at launch. Windows Central
  2. Boxed-edition buyers say their code is missing or already redeemed. According to VGTimes, some physical-edition buyers say their box has an already redeemed code or none at all. With no disc, no code means no install. Rockstar hadn't commented as of that report. VGTimes
  3. PS5 codes are region-locked and Japanese ones expire. Physical PS5 codes only work on a PlayStation Network account from the same region they were sold in. According to Dexerto, Japanese codes expire 170 days after launch; Insider Gaming says Xbox isn't region-locked. Insider Gaming

item.title: GTA VI gets its first mandatory patch five days before launch
item.description:
Mandatory patch 1.002.000, a 24-hour YouTube marathon, lighter versions in Japan and Australia, codes visible through some boxes and the GTA VI effect on the economy.

  1. Patch 1.002.000 is here and it's mandatory. Rockstar released the first update on November 13: about 1.07 GB on PS5 and 2.18 GB on Xbox Series. It's required to play on the 19th and has no patch notes. It rolled out in stages and reached everyone by 23:00 UTC. tbreak
  2. YouTube will stream 24 straight hours of GTA VI on launch day. It starts November 19 at 12:00 a.m. ET (6:00 a.m. in Spain), with an RDCWorld pre-show the night before. More than 30 creators will play live and it wraps up from Miami. KeenGamer
  3. The preload is smaller in Japan and Australia. According to Kotaku, the Japanese version is about 1.2 GB smaller and the Australia and New Zealand version is missing a file of roughly 704 KB. People fear censorship, but Rockstar hasn't confirmed any cuts. Kotaku
  4. Some physical boxes reveal the code with a flashlight. VideoCardz reports that on certain physical editions (which are a code in a box) the download code can be read without opening it. Tests on US and UK copies failed; some European ones may be less protected. VideoCardz
  5. CNBC: GTA VI may show up in food delivery, tourism and time off. CNBC looks at how the launch on the 19th could boost food delivery orders, vacation days taken and even tourism in Miami. CNBC
